messages:
igor: Quick follow-up from the rollout metadata chat — I prototyped adding a `compatibility` vector to pin records so runtime can pick a fallback model variant without hard-coding mapping. Thoughts?

marta: can you sketch the fields? curious how this differs from `fallback_order` we already have.

igor: Sure. Idea is a list of capability tags + minimum interface guarantees, e.g. `[{\"capability\":\"structured-output-v2\", \"min_contract\":\"schema-v1\", \"score\":0.9}]`. Runtime selects the highest-scored variant matching request constraints.

liz: I like intent. Two quick concerns: 1) how do we keep this compact for the common fast-path (latency SLOs)? 2) how do we prevent config drift across Dedicated/Private installs?

phil: for (1) we can default to an integer bitmask for micro-optimizations (fast-path) and expand to full JSON for diagnostic/rollout UIs. for (2) expose a compact version with a hash and store full semantics in control-plane only.

jen: pinging @deploy-bot — does deploy history currently include model variant hash we could reference?

deploy-bot: build-9312 deployed model-hub://redwood/gpt-small@sha256:abcd1234 to eu-west-1 at 2024-06-15T17:02:11Z

marta: That metadata gives us a reliable anchor. If pin stores `variant_hash` plus our `compatibility` vector, runtime fallback is deterministic. But we should define an upgrade path for pinned models when semantics change (e.g., schema-v1 -> schema-v2).

igor: Proposal for schema evolution: each `compatibility` entry gets an `epoch` and `migration_hint` field. When runtime sees pinned model lacking a required capability, it consults the hint to locate an approved replacement or to trigger rate-limited canary routing.

liz: Migration hints sound useful but risky. Need auditability + operator opt-in for Private installs. Suggest `migration_hint` be optional and require explicit enterprise policy to allow auto-migrate.

phil: Agree. Add `policy_allow_auto_migrate: boolean` at the pin-level. Default false for private deployments, true for hosted.

jen: Operational checklist: 1) telemetry events when runtime uses `compatibility` fallback; 2) alert if fallback rate > X% for a route; 3) UI to preview target variant and rollback.

igor: yes. Also add an immutable `pin_origin` (ui, api, onboarding-script) and `pin_audit_id` so we can trace why a pin exists.

marta: One more: we should standardize capability vocab — a small enum-first list (structured-output, long-context, multimodal, safety-filtered) and allow extensible freeform tags for experiments.

phil: Implementation notes: storage row schema can be: `pin_id | variant_hash | origin | audit_id | pack_version | compatibility_blob | allow_auto_migrate | created_at` where `compatibility_blob` is JSONB in the control plane and a compact base64 representation in client bundles.

liz: Question: how will this interact with A/B rollouts? If we have two variants with overlapping compatibilities, we need deterministic tie-breaker (weight, score, created_at).

igor: tie-breaker order: explicit `weight` if present, else `score`, else `created_at` descending. We'll document precedence.

jen: sounds good. Can we put a short example pin record for docs?

igor: Example:

```\n{\n  \"pin_id\": \"pin-20240615-17\",\n  \"variant_hash\": \"sha256:abcd1234\",\n  \"origin\": \"api\",\n  \"audit_id\": \"audit-789\",\n  \"pack_version\": \"v1\",\n  \"compatibility_blob\": [\n    {\"capability\":\"structured-output-v2\",\"min_contract\":\"schema-v1\",\"score\":0.95,\"epoch\":1},\n    {\"capability\":\"long-context\",\"min_contract\":\"ctx-2048\",\"score\":0.7,\"epoch\":1}\n  ],\n  \"allow_auto_migrate\": false,\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-06-15T17:02:11Z\"\n}\n```

marta: Nice. Next steps? I can draft an RFC update with these fields + migration policy language.

phil: I'll take storage/fast-path sketch and a perf micro-benchmark for JSONB vs bitmask lookup.

liz: I'll draft control-plane upgrade notes and enterprise opt-in UI copy.

igor: Great — assign owners and let's reconvene next Tue. Thanks all :thumbsup:
